newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan tells Lima of fears about Peru police moves.
newsitem.headline: Japan tells Lima of fears about Peru police moves.

text.p: Japan has expressed its concern to Peru over the tightening of the guard around the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima, a senior Foreign Ministry official said on Monday.

"The Japanese government has conveyed its concern that an unforeseen event that could erupt around the ambassador's official residence at anytime should not hamper earnest efforts toward a prompt conclusion of the hostage crisis," Vice Foreign Minister Sadayuki Hayashi told a news conference.
Peruvian police have thrown stones and garbage into the grounds, flown helicopters overhead and moved in armoured vehicles and men with high-powered rifles and night-vision equipment.

In response to what they called provocative movements by police, the Tupac Amaru guerrillas holding 72 hostages fired warning shots into the air following several tense days outside the besieged compound.

Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto told reporters earlier on Monday he feared Peruvian police authorities' moves to tighten security could have a detrimental effect on the safety of those held captive inside the diplomatic mansion.

"I'm worrying how it may affect the hostages inside. I'm wondering if I can ask...the Peruvian government not to go too far. Not thinking of the hostages' mental state may have an adverse effect," Hashimoto said.
On Sunday, the guerrillas freed an ailing police commander from the ambassador's residence so that he could receive medical treatment.
